topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview of cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the learning objectives regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional therapies, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard non-targeted cancer treatment modalities alongside the fundamental limitations of systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including signaling dependencies, checkpoint deficiencies, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on small-molecule inhibition of oncogenic driver kinases and the diverse molecular mechanisms tumors use to develop resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the design and therapeutic mechanisms of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates targeted to tumor surface proteins.

topics.label: Immunotherapy and cellular immune targeting
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address approaches for harnessing and re-engineering the host immune system to recognize and destroy tumor cells.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on the systemic challenges, historical progress, and future clinical directions in cancer management.
